gen-gf-paprika-fs-rowan: Big, loud, crowded lowercase: Paprika fills the line like capitals, scattered wide and hollow inside. Rowan, a classic serif, is the one that wants to be read, with generous curves and moderate height.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-almendra: Paprika's lowercase swells up to fill the line like capitals, spaced wide apart. Almendra, a text serif with a deep midsection, settles underneath and gives the shouting a bookish, dignified answer.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-bree-serif: Commanding from the first word, Paprika spreads its capital-sized lowercase wide, while Bree Serif, a classic serif, comes in refined and oversized. Give the heading more size than the text.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-port-lligat-slab: Loud, scattered, expressive lettering up top. Port Lligat Slab follows with porthole-wide counters and curves left open, so paragraphs feel traditional and unhurried.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-quando: Quando spreads sparse, wide letter spacing and a tall middle zone through every word, giving a bookish, traditional text serif. Paprika's commanding heading above it keeps the page lively.
gen-gf-phudu-author: Author brings a refined serif voice, with a slight swell on the bowls and a dignified manner. Phudu's heading curves stay thin-free, so Author can be sized a touch larger to carry the page.
gen-gf-phudu-cabin: Bold, distinctive Phudu draws its curves with a plain ballpoint line and open terminals. Cabin follows, warm and clean, its bent-tubing sans letterforms feeling like a close cousin to that pen-like heading.
gen-gf-phudu-dm-sans: Phudu's tubular, wire-like letterforms are the first thing you notice, bold and open at every curve. And DM Sans, approachable and friendly with wide-set terminals on s, quietly carries the rest.
gen-gf-phudu-fs-paquito: Chunky, pen-smooth headings with no hairline strokes. Phudu draws a bold lowercase a, while Paquito, a serif of confident, approachable build, sits lower with a minimal gap between x-height and caps.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-aleo: Aleo reads dignified and classic, its counters letting the eye slip in and out. Phudu, drawn like a fixed-width nib, supplies the bold, distinctive heading while Aleo, a classic serif, handles the text.
